identity.product_promise: A standalone local/browser texture-authoring tool for deterministic shader tiles, multi-channel materials and original native pixel terrain, with portable exports.
primary_use_cases: Inspect channel, repeat, seam and terrain connectivity behavior
Bake and export reviewed original textures
non_goals: Credential and broker operations as product behavior
A second product tree or framework migration
Artwork acceptance from technical proof alone

what: A standalone local/browser texture-authoring tool for deterministic shader tiles, multi-channel materials and original native pixel terrain, with portable exports.
why: Give texture and sprite authoring one Gknome identity around the standalone Vite app and portable static builds.
how: Keep actual product implementation in src/ and existing npm scripts.
Use project-owned Gknome operations and a bounded argument-array adapter; do not launch background services during onboarding.
Use selective Summary Bank groups and keep credential-bearing auth source outside context packing.
Use the reviewed local Gknome publisher with explicit paths and separate clean-proof/push boundaries; no implicit remote creation.
Exclude accounts/connectors/database behavior from the standalone product; keep repository publication credentials separate and operator-owned.

in: Selective product and foundation context routes
Foundation guidance and safe publication handoff
out: Unreviewed provenance or source-control history rewriting

safety: Preserve staged/modified/untracked owner work and secret guard failures.
Require explicit publication arguments; never substitute raw Git push.
courtesy: Keep existing npm/Vite/env/hosting commands and paths.
show: Distinguish static foundation proof, executed focused product checks and unrun visual acceptance.
efficiency: Use bounded groups, existing tests and synchronous checks; no duplicate product tree.

done_when: Identity, typed metadata and source roots describe the existing standalone app.
Declared operations reach real npm commands through supported dispatch.
Semantic contracts, selective context audit and the focused product check pass without credential contents in context.
Publication uses explicit reviewed task scope and the qualified local helper, preserves security guards and named deletions, and follows required local proof.
